newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telefonica CEO aims to exand international activity - paper.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica CEO aims to exand international activity - paper.

text.p: Spanish telecommunications group Telefonica de Espana aims to achieve half of its sales through international activities in the future, the company's chairman was quoted as saying in a German newspaper on Friday.
The Spanish government is preparing to sell off its remaining 20.9 percent stake in the company, which will put it among the first western European telephone company to be fully privatised.

Telefonica chief Juan Villalonga told the economic daily Handelsblatt that the company was particularly interested in expanding in Asia and that he was "very optimistic" about the company's prospects.

"In two to four years we want to achieve around half our turnover abroad," Villanova said, adding that he ranked Telefonica as Europe's fifth largest telecommunications company and number nine worldwide.
Villalonga said Telefonica had a good chance of competing against larger telecommunications companies for business in Asia.
"Governments and enterprises in Asia often see the the big telephone companies as too dominant. They don't think entrepreneurial enough," he said.

Villalonga said the company was also interested in the German market. It has a partnership through its involvement in the Unisource consortium with Mannesmann, which is one of the strongest local rivals to Deutsche Telekom.
He said the Telefonica administrative council would meet in Germany in May, but Handelsblatt said there was no confirmation of talks with Deutsche Telekom.
Telefonica is in talks with AT&T, GTE, SBC Communications, Bell Atlantic and MCI Communications about partnership in the United States.
"A decision should be made on this by the end of February," he said.

Telefonica also has activities in Romania but has no current plans to expand elsewhere in eastern Europe. However, Villalonga said the company wants to exploit its traditional ties to Africa and mentioned plans to begin in Morocco.
